WIN-HGO-S5-20261009 report (goldfish-deep, Sonnet 5.5 / xhigh). Implementation complete, committed eba5e5a11b933ce5696e48b67bb92a345f16b4e3. Independent review: pending. PO acceptance pending.

Route pre-check: class is test-only (QG-04), not A/G/S. Requested route (field 6): goldfish-deep, tool-layer model sonnet (Sonnet 5.5, effort xhigh). Observed (this dispatch's runtime prompt): 'Sonnet 5.5 ... claude-sonnet-5-5'. No contradiction. GUARD-BOOTSTRAP-RECEIPT-MISSING fired once on the first Write; the named preflight ran once (exit 0), then the identical write succeeded.

1. DoD results
- Per-chunk native captures, every targeted case green or typed-skipped: passed. Final-state chunk-2: pass 4, fail 0, skipped 7 (typed), wrapped exit 0.
- WSL capture of the same chunk, no change: passed. pass 11, fail 0, skipped 0, wrapped exit 0 (counts read from the artifact).
- One commit of the two test files with the prescribed subject: passed (eba5e5a11b933ce5696e48b67bb92a345f16b4e3, 2 files, 23 insertions, 11 deletions).
- Terminal record evidence/dispatch-record-WIN-HGO-S5-20261009.json: written (this file).
Per goal item: S1 four symlink cases: typed skip natively (symlink probe EPERM on this host), bodies pass under WSL. CROSSREPOGUIDANCE-1a/1b: join(...) around the git toplevel at both assert.equal(recorded.root, ...) lines, native pass, plan.root assertion untouched. Recovery-guard case: native pass (40.6 s), WSL pass. NVA-HGOFIX-2 lib x3 and script x1: see section 5.

Recovery-guard verdict (briefing condition: confirm the live-owner design first). Trace: the nested acquireAuditLock inside afterRecoveryGuardFn enters clearAbandonedAuditRecovery because the recovery guard exists; its owner is this live process; win32AuditLockOwnerState never answers 'live' by documented design (no per-process start identity); so HGO-AUDIT-LOCK-AMBIGUOUS is thrown at the 'state !== dead' line BEFORE any rename, the guard stays in place and the outer call still returns recovered:true with the protected bytes unchanged. The second half of the case needs nothing: the nested call there finds no recovery file and no lock, and the outer HGO-AUDIT-LOCK-CHANGED comes from the !sameLockIdentity clause, which short-circuits before any owner-state read. Verdict: test fault, same design as the held-lock case; not a product fault. Edit: the expected code is platform-conditional (AMBIGUOUS on win32, RECOVERY-BUSY elsewhere), mirroring heldLockCode. No assertion added, removed or weakened.

2. Evidence (repo-root-relative; evidence/ is git-ignored)
- evidence/WIN-HGO-S5-20261009/chunk-2-lib-and-script-final.txt: node plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/capture-evidence.mjs --label WIN-HGO-S5-chunk-2 --out <that path> -- node --test <7 x --test-name-pattern: 'security and authority boundaries', 'NVA-W4-01B', 'pipeline author repair binds', 'NOVA-HGOELIG-4', 'a recovery guard excludes', 'NVA-HGOFIX-2', 'NVA-CROSSREPOGUIDANCE-1'> plugins/pipeline-core/lib/human-guard-override.test.mjs plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/guard-human-override.test.mjs ; native Windows ; wrapped exit 0 ; pass 4 / fail 0 / skipped 7.
- evidence/WIN-HGO-S5-20261009/wsl-chunk-1-lib-and-script.txt: the same command under wsl.exe -e bash -lc 'cd <repo-root-in-wsl>; ...' ; wrapped exit 0 ; pass 11 / fail 0 / skipped 0.
- evidence/WIN-HGO-S5-20261009/chunk-1-lib-and-script.txt: discovery capture before the last edit; native; wrapped exit 1 ; pass 3 / fail 1 / skipped 7. The one red was NVA-HGOFIX-2 eligibility() Bash argv-token case (assert eligible === true, actual false: default platform is win32 on this host). Kept as the trail for why that case changed.

3. Changed files (commit eba5e5a11b933ce5696e48b67bb92a345f16b4e3)
- plugins/pipeline-core/lib/human-guard-override.test.mjs: S1 skip DIRECTORY_SYMLINK_SKIP on four tests; join(...) at the two CROSSREPOGUIDANCE root assertions; recovery-guard expected code per platform; NVA-HGOFIX-2 separatorNormalized/safePath and crossBoundaryTarget cases typed-skipped on win32 via the existing POSIX_BACKSLASH_SKIP; NVA-HGOFIX-2 eligibility() Bash case passes explicit { platform: 'linux' } for its POSIX arm.
- plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/guard-human-override.test.mjs: NVA-HGOFIX-2 backslash-name case typed-skipped on win32 (inline skip option with reason).
Untracked or git-ignored, not committed: evidence/WIN-HGO-S5-20261009/*.txt, this record, scratch/commit-msg/WIN-HGO-S5-20261009.txt, scratch/finalize-WIN-HGO-S5.mjs.

4. Deliberately not changed
- All production files (forbidden). No assertion weakened or removed; POSIX behaviour of every touched test is byte-identical (skips are false off win32, the explicit platform equals the POSIX default, join() is a no-op on POSIX).
- The author-repair case ('pipeline author repair binds ...') still compares a git --show-toplevel result directly (around the original line 2137). It is gated by the S1 skip here. On a Developer-Mode host where the symlink probe passes it may go red for the same separator reason as CROSSREPOGUIDANCE. Not verifiable on this host; NOT fixed.
- Cost of the typed skips: the win32-injection arms inside the two skipped NVA-HGOFIX-2 lib cases (separatorNormalized with platform win32, safePath and crossBoundaryTarget forced to win32) now run only on POSIX hosts, not natively; WSL (pass 11) covers them.
- The foreign uncommitted edits (pipeline-state.mjs, po-human-approval.mjs, sanctioned-args-onboarding.mjs, pipeline-state.test.mjs) were never staged or touched; the commit used exact pathspecs and lists only the two test files.
- The rest of the 6000-line lib file was not run natively (targeted chunks only, per the Windows rule); other reds in the original 20 not named in this slice were not re-measured.

5. Deviations from spec
- NVA-HGOFIX-2 lib cases (separatorNormalized/safePath, crossBoundaryTarget): the briefing said 'pass an explicit platform'; I used a typed skip (POSIX_BACKSLASH_SKIP) instead. Grounds: the platform seam reaches separatorNormalized() only; resolve() and relative() in crossBoundaryTarget/safePath are the host path module, so with platform linux on win32 relative() returns a backslash path, the escape check (rel.startsWith('../')) does not recognise it and crossBoundaryTarget returns null, so the case still fails. The safePath fixture also does mkdirSync(join(root, '..\hgofix-seam')), which on NTFS creates a directory OUTSIDE root that the finally block never removes. The native-reds note (section C) names the skip alternative. The third NVA-HGOFIX-2 lib case (eligibility Bash) did take the explicit platform, as briefed.
- Those NVA-HGOFIX-2 cases live in the LIB test file (three of them); the script file holds one. The briefing text placed them under the script file. Both files were in scope, so no scope burst.
- Script-file backslash case: briefing said typed skip; done. There is no NTFS fixture to create there (it is a platform-seam call), but the default-platform arm only exists on POSIX, so the skip is correct.
- One failed attempt: the 4th NVA-HGOFIX-2 lib case (eligibility Bash) was red on the first native capture (not in the native-reds table) and green after one edit; a single failure, not a stop condition. The advisor was consulted twice (before edits, before closing).
- Budget: the 80 % notice fired on call 44, after all edits and both captures were done; later calls were the WSL count read, staging, commit, record writes and the closing advisor consult. No edit was made after the notice.

6. Open items
- independent review: pending (only the Elephant may dispatch the Critic). PO acceptance pending. Not a closing-allowance handover: all briefed work is committed and verified.
- For the dispatcher: whether to schedule a Developer-Mode native run so the four S1 bodies and the author-repair show-toplevel comparison are measured natively (they are typed-skipped here and pass under WSL).
- No triggered stop condition, no briefing defect beyond the file-placement wording noted in section 5.
